findings.title: A command reply that fails to parse kills the Listener, and the send() waiting for it hangs forever (aclose() cannot release it either)
findings.bug_class: exception-handling / exception escapes a loop and hangs a caller
findings.scenario: Any tab.send()/connection.send() whose result the generated cdp parser rejects. This happens when Chrome's protocol differs from the bundled cdp: a required key is missing (KeyError), or there is a new enum value, e.g. a cookie sameSite value unknown to CookieSameSite (ValueError). listener_loop pops the Transaction from conn.mapper and then calls tx(**message) outside any try. Inside Transaction.__call__, cdp_obj.send(result) raises something other than StopIteration, and the exception leaves listener_loop, so the listener task dies. The Future is never resolved. It is already gone from mapper, so _fail_pending_transactions in aclose()/_detach_session can never fail it, and send() hangs forever. Its own explicit `raise ProtocolException('could not parse the cdp response')` also kills the listener instead of failing the tx. On the browser connection this also starves every flat-session tab, because no one reads the websocket until another browser-level send() creates a new Listener. Event parsing on the same loop does catch these errors (parse_json_event in try/except -> logger.info; continue), which shows the intended behaviour.
findings.why_tests_miss: tests/core/test_connection.py has one test (concurrent aopen). No test feeds a malformed or schema-drifted reply. Real-Chrome tests use a Chrome that matches the bundled cdp.
findings.repro_idea: Run a fake websockets.serve peer that answers Target.getTargetInfo with {"id":N,"result":{}}. Call conn.send(cdp.target.get_target_info()) as a task, wait 3s, then call conn.aclose() and check that the task is still pending. Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/detect-B15/probe_tx_parse.py and probe_tx_parse2.py
findings.evidence: probe_tx_parse.py printed: 'send done within 3s: False | listener running: False | listener exc: KeyError('targetInfo')' with the task stuck at connection.py:662 `return await tx`. The same happened for Storage.getCookies with sameSite 'SomeFutureValue': listener exc ValueError("'SomeFutureValue' is not a valid CookieSameSite"). probe_tx_parse2.py: 'after aclose(): send finished? False | tx in mapper: 0'. The only trace is 'Task exception was never retrieved' at GC. Related to the known 'listener only catches Timeout/Cancelled/ConnectionClosed' lead, but this site is outside that try. The fix belongs in result dispatch (tx.set_exception), and the tx is lost permanently.

findings.title: Cancelling or failing Browser.start() after Chrome is spawned leaks the Chrome process and its temp profile, even after the event loop ends
findings.bug_class: cancellation handling / missing cleanup on exception
findings.scenario: `await asyncio.wait_for(zendriver.start(headless=True), 1)`, or Ctrl-C (asyncio.run cancels the main task), or any exception from start() after util._start_process. Examples: set_discover_targets/update_targets/_read_headless_user_agent raising, or CancelledError while it polls test_connection. start() has no try/except/finally to stop the process it spawned. Browser.create registers asyncio_atexit cleanup only after `await instance.start()` returns, so nothing ever terminates Chrome or removes the temporary --user-data-dir. The Browser also stays in util.get_registered_instances() for good.
findings.why_tests_miss: tests/core/test_browser.py::test_connection_error_raises_exception_and_logs_stderr covers only the 'never connected' branch, which calls stop() itself. No test cancels or times out start().
findings.repro_idea: Spy on util._start_process to capture the Popen. Run `await asyncio.wait_for(zd.start(headless=True), 0.05)`, let asyncio.run() return, then check p.poll() is None and that the user-data-dir still exists. Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/detect-B15/probe_start_cancel.py
findings.evidence: probe_start_cancel.py output: '0.05 timed out ... pid 3291 still running: True ... alive after asyncio.run returned: [3291] ... profile dir exists: True'. Starts that were not cancelled were cleaned up normally (still running: False, profile dir exists: False).

findings.title: Browser.stop() hangs forever on an unresponsive browser, because the CDP detach/close steps have no timeout and the terminate/kill fallback comes after them
findings.bug_class: cleanup path blocks forever / kill fallback unreachable
findings.scenario: The Chrome browser process stops responding (hung or suspended) and the user calls `await browser.stop()`. _stop first awaits `target.aclose()` for every target. For attached tabs that sends Target.detachFromTarget through the browser connection and awaits the reply with no timeout. Then it awaits `self.connection.send(cdp.browser.close())`, also with no timeout. The 3s terminate -> kill fallback is never reached, so stop() never returns. If the caller wraps it in wait_for, the cancellation leaves the process running and the profile undeleted.
findings.why_tests_miss: test_pending_commands_fail_when_browser_process_dies / ..._connection_is_closed suspend the process but call connection.aclose() and then resume or kill it. They never call browser.stop() while Chrome is unresponsive. test_browser_stop_exits_gracefully_without_kill uses a healthy browser.
findings.repro_idea: Start a headless browser and attach a tab (tab.evaluate('1')). Send SIGSTOP to browser._process.pid, then run `await asyncio.wait_for(browser.stop(), 10)`. It times out, and task.print_stack() shows it waiting on Target.detachFromTarget. Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/detect-B15/probe_stop_hang.py, probe_stop_hang2.py
findings.evidence: probe_stop_hang.py printed: 'stop() did not return within 10s (terminate/kill fallback never reached)' and 'process still alive: True'. probe_stop_hang2.py stack: Browser.stop() at browser.py:872 waiting on 'Transaction method: Target.detachFromTarget status: pending'.

findings.title: One event handler that raises when called (e.g. wrong arity) kills the Listener through an explicit re-raise, so commands already in flight hang
findings.bug_class: exception re-raised inside dispatch loop
findings.scenario: A user registers `async def on_target(): ...` (no parameters) via browser.connection.add_handler(cdp.target.TargetCreated, on_target) or tab.add_handler(...). _accepts_connection_argument returns False, so the loop calls callback(event), which raises TypeError synchronously while the coroutine object is created. The dispatch block logs a warning and then `raise`s (the outer `except Exception: raise` passes it on too), so the listener task dies. The reply to a command that is already in flight, and is queued right behind the event, is never read: that send() hangs until some later send() happens to create a new Listener. Every other handler for every event also stops firing. On the browser connection this starves all flat-session tabs, since nothing reads the shared websocket.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test registers a handler whose signature does not fit. Handler tests use well-formed lambdas and coroutines.
findings.repro_idea: Run a fake CDP peer that, for Browser.getVersion, first sends a Target.targetCreated event and then the reply. Register a good handler plus `async def bad(): pass`, then call conn.send(cdp.browser.get_version()) with a 3s timeout. Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/detect-B15/probe_bad_handler.py
findings.evidence: probe_bad_handler.py printed: 'get_version finished within 3s: False' and 'listener running: False exc: TypeError('main.<locals>.bad_handler() takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given')'. This is a distinct site from the known receive-side lead: the loop raises on purpose after logging, rather than isolating the faulty callback.

findings.title: Browser.__aexit__ and Connection/Tab.__aexit__ replace the user's exception with exc_type(exc_val): TypeError for multi-arg exceptions and ExceptionGroup, wrong exit status for sys.exit, and ProtocolException.code lost
findings.bug_class: __aexit__ changes the exception
findings.function: Browser.__aexit__ (also Connection.__aexit__ at zendriver/core/connection.py:599, inherited by Tab)
findings.scenario: The documented pattern `async with await zd.start() as browser:` (examples/wait_for_page.py, expect_download.py), or `async with tab:`. When the body raises, __aexit__ runs `raise exc_type(exc_val)` instead of returning and letting Python re-raise. (1) json.loads('{bad') in the body: the caller gets TypeError("JSONDecodeError.__init__() missing 2 required positional arguments"), so `except json.JSONDecodeError` no longer matches. The same happens for UnicodeDecodeError, CalledProcessError, IncompleteReadError and websockets ConnectionClosed. (2) A failing asyncio.TaskGroup in the body: TypeError('BaseExceptionGroup.__new__() takes exactly 2 arguments'), and except* no longer matches. (3) sys.exit(3) in the body: SystemExit(SystemExit(3)) prints '3' and the process exits with status 1. (4) ProtocolException({'code':-32000,...}) comes back with code=None and the code folded into the message.
findings.why_tests_miss: tests/conftest.py's CreateBrowser has its own __aexit__. Tests only enter `async with create_browser(...)`, never `async with browser:` / `async with tab:` with a failing body.
findings.repro_idea: In `async with browser:` run json.loads('{x'), a failing TaskGroup, or raise ProtocolException({'code':-32000,'message':'m'}), and print the type and .code the caller sees. Separately, a script with `async with Browser-like: sys.exit(3)` exits with $? = 1. Probes: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/detect-B15/probe_aexit.py and probe_sysexit.py
findings.evidence: probe_aexit.py (py3.13.16): '[Browser] json: caller sees TypeError: "JSONDecodeError.__init__() missing 2 required positional arguments..."', '[Browser] group: caller sees TypeError: BaseExceptionGroup.__new__() takes exactly 2 arguments (1 given)', '[Browser] proto: ... code=None', '[Tab] json: caller sees TypeError ...'. probe_sysexit.py printed '3' and 'exit status: 1', while plain sys.exit(3) gives status 3. The code has been unchanged since the initial import (5c1a005).

findings.title: Element.click() (and mouse_click/mouse_move/mouse_drag/flash/screenshot_b64) raises a bare Exception on display:none elements: get_position never returns None, so every 'not visible' fallback is dead code
findings.bug_class: wrong exception raised / caller's None-handling unreachable
findings.scenario: `btn = await tab.select('#hidden-button'); await btn.click()` on a display:none element, e.g. a hidden <input type=file> or a visually hidden checkbox. click() calls `await self.flash(0.25)` before the JS `el.click()`. flash() calls get_position(), and Chrome returns empty content quads, so get_position runs `raise Exception('could not find position ...')`. Its `except IndexError: return None` is unreachable, because quads[0] only runs when quads is non-empty. flash()'s `if pos is None: warn; return` never triggers, and the exception escapes click(), so the JS click, which would work on a hidden element, is never sent. mouse_click/mouse_move/mouse_drag ('could not find location ..., not clicking') and screenshot_b64 (documented RuntimeError) also get a generic Exception instead of their graceful branch or documented type.
findings.why_tests_miss: Click and mouse tests in tests/core (test_tab.py, test_keyinputs.py, test_frames.py, test_mouse.py) only use visible elements. Nothing exercises hidden or zero-size elements.
findings.repro_idea: Open the page data:text/html,<button id=hid style="display:none" onclick="window.c=1">. Run `await (await tab.select('#hid')).click()`: it raises Exception, and window.c stays undefined. document.getElementById('hid').click() works. Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/detect-B15/probe_hidden_click.py, probe_swallow.py
findings.evidence: probe_hidden_click.py printed: "hidden click raised: Exception 'could not find position for <button id=\"hid\" style=\"display:none\" ...'", 'JS el.click would have worked; clicked_hid = None', 'mouse_click raised: Exception ...', 'screenshot_b64 raised: Exception (docstring promises RuntimeError)'. probe_swallow.py: 'direct JS click on hidden el sets flag: 1'.

findings.title: Element.query_selector_all / query_selector silently swallow every ProtocolException except 'could not find node' (e.g. invalid selector -> [] / None)
findings.bug_class: swallowed error the caller needs
findings.function: Tab.query_selector_all / Tab.query_selector (the _node branch, reached from Element.query_selector_all / Element.query_selector)
findings.scenario: `box = await tab.select('#box'); await box.query_selector_all('span[[')` returns [], and box.query_selector('span[[') returns None. In the `except ProtocolException` handler, the `_node is not None` branch only handles 'could not find node' and has no else/raise. Any other DOM error falls through to `if not node_ids: return []` (or `return None`). The same invalid selector at tab level (`tab.query_selector_all('span[[')`) correctly raises ProtocolException('DOM Error while querying'). A selector typo or any other DOM error therefore looks like 'no such element', silently, for element-scoped queries.
findings.why_tests_miss: Tests only use valid selectors. No test calls an element-scoped query with a selector or node Chrome rejects for a reason other than a stale node.
findings.repro_idea: Compare tab.query_selector_all('span[[') (raises) with (await tab.select('#box')).query_selector_all('span[[') (returns []). Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/detect-B15/probe_swallow.py
findings.evidence: probe_swallow.py printed: 'tab.query_selector_all invalid -> raises ProtocolException: DOM Error while querying', 'box.query_selector_all invalid -> []', 'box.query_selector invalid -> None'. The query_selector equivalent is at tab.py:649.

findings.title: Element.apply drops JavaScript exceptions: a throwing function returns None, and the exception_details branch is dead
findings.bug_class: error dropped where the caller needs it
findings.scenario: `await elem.apply("(e) => { throw new Error('boom') }")` returns None, the same as a function returning undefined. Runtime.callFunctionOn returns (RemoteObject of the thrown error, ExceptionDetails). result[0] is always a truthy RemoteObject, so `if result and result[0]: return result[0].value` returns the error object's value (None). `elif result[1]: return result[1]` can never run. Callers built on apply (clear_input, React value setters, user scripts) cannot detect failures, while Tab.evaluate raises ProtocolException(errors) for the same JS.
findings.why_tests_miss: The only apply test (test_react_controlled_input.py:113) uses a function that does not throw.
findings.repro_idea: On any page: `await (await tab.select('div')).apply("(e)=>{throw new Error('x')}")` returns None. Compare with tab.evaluate of a throwing IIFE, which raises. Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/detect-B15/probe_swallow.py
findings.evidence: probe_swallow.py printed 'box.apply(throwing fn) returned: None' and 'tab.evaluate(throwing) -> raises ProtocolException (for contrast)'. Confidence is medium because the code may have meant to return rather than raise the details, but even that path is dead.

findings.title: expect_request/expect_response: two matching requests in one burst cause InvalidStateError in a handler task and make .response/.response_body belong to a different request than .request
findings.bug_class: unhandled exception in handler task (set_result on done future) + state overwrite
findings.scenario: `async with tab.expect_response(r'.*\.json') as exp:` while the page fires two matching fetches together, e.g. Promise.all([fetch('a.json'), fetch('b.json')]). Both Network.requestWillBeSent events are drained back-to-back. On Python 3.12+, wait_for/Queue.get do not yield when data is already buffered. The listener schedules _request_handler twice before the first task can call _remove_request_handler. Task 1 sets request_id=R1 and resolves request_future. Task 2 overwrites request_id=R2, then set_result raises InvalidStateError ('Task exception was never retrieved'). response_future then resolves with R2's ResponseReceived, so exp.request is a.json but exp.response/response_body are b.json. DownloadExpectation._handler and BaseFetchInterception._response_handler have the same unguarded set_result.
findings.why_tests_miss: test_tab.py expect_* tests navigate to a single matching URL, so only one event ever matches.
findings.repro_idea: Run a fake CDP peer that, after one reply, sends requestWillBeSent(R1,a.json), requestWillBeSent(R2,b.json), responseReceived(R1), responseReceived(R2) in one burst. Await exp.request and exp.response and compare the URLs. Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/detect-B15/probe_expect_race.py
findings.evidence: probe_expect_race.py (py3.13.16) printed: 'expectation .request url : http://x/a.json', 'expectation .response url: http://x/b.json | request_id: R2', "unhandled task errors: [\"InvalidStateError('invalid state')\"]". Not yet probed on 3.10/3.11, where wait_for's inner task may yield and hide the race.

findings.title: One shared ProtocolException instance is set on all pending transactions, and every send() appends its own command to it, so each caller's error lists other calls' commands
findings.bug_class: exception object mutated across callers
findings.scenario: Three concurrent sends are pending and the connection is closed (aclose(), session detach, browser.stop()). _fail_pending_transactions sets the same ProtocolException('connection was closed') on every tx. Each awaiting send() then does `e.message += '\ncommand:...params:...'` on that shared object and re-raises it. Every caller receives an identical exception whose message lists all three commands, and the list grows with the number of pending calls, so the error points at the wrong command.
findings.why_tests_miss: test_pending_commands_fail_when_connection_is_closed has only one pending command and checks only the type.
findings.repro_idea: Run a fake peer that never answers, start 3 sends, call aclose(), and print str() of each result. Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/detect-B15/probe_shared_exc.py
findings.evidence:
probe_shared_exc.py printed the same string three times: 'connection was closed
command:Browser.getVersion
params:[]
command:Page.reload
params:{}
command:DOM.getDocument
params:{}', and 'same instance: True'.

findings.title: (Outside B15's bug class, found while reading) Tab.__call__ passes text and selector to wait_for in swapped positions, so tab(text=...) never finds text
findings.bug_class: argument order (not exception handling)
findings.scenario: `await tab(text='Hello world')` calls `self.wait_for(text, selector, timeout)` positionally, but the signature is wait_for(selector=None, text=None, timeout=10). The text is used as a CSS selector ('Hello world' matches no element), the call polls for the full timeout and raises TimeoutError('time ran out while waiting') even though the text is on the page. tab(selector='button') only appears to work because DOM.performSearch also matches tag names.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test or doc calls the Tab object directly.
findings.repro_idea:
Load data:text/html,

Hello world

. tab.wait_for(text='Hello world', timeout=2) finds it, and `await tab(text='Hello world', timeout=2)` raises TimeoutError. Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/detect-B15/probe_call.py
findings.evidence:
probe_call.py printed: 'tab.wait_for(text=...) ->

Hello world

' and "tab(text='Hello world') -> TimeoutError: time ran out while waiting". The positional swap has been present since dd9a4f8 (the call previously lacked await but had the same order).

coverage.read_in_depth: zendriver/core/connection.py: Transaction, ProtocolException, Connection.aopen/_attach_session/_detach_session/_fail_pending_transactions/aclose/wait/__aexit__/send/_send_transaction/_receive_message/_send_oneshot/_prepare_headless, and the full Listener. zendriver/core/browser.py: create, start, test_connection, _get_tab, update_targets, _handle_target_update, get, create_context, __aexit__, __next__, stop/_stop, _cleanup_temporary_profile, CookieJar, HTTPApi. All of expect.py and intercept.py. proxy.py: open_tunnel, the forwarder, pipe, copy_stream. cloudflare.py: verify_cf and challenge detection. tab.py: disable_dom_agent, get_frames/_search_frames, find/select/find_all/select_all/xpath, query_selector(_all), find_elements_by_text, evaluate, close, wait_for, wait_for_ready_state, mouse_* helpers, set_local_storage, __call__. element.py: __getattr__/__setattr__, update, click, apply, get_position, mouse_click/move/drag, screenshot_b64, flash, resolve_node. util.py: _start_process, _read_process_stderr, cdp_get_module. Every except/finally/raise in zendriver/core was grepped and triaged. Probes ran against real headless Chromium and fake websockets CDP peers on Python 3.13.16.
coverage.not_covered: I did not probe Python 3.10/3.11-specific behaviour: the asyncio.TimeoutError vs builtin TimeoutError split (cloudflare.verify_cf raises builtin TimeoutError while the rest of the library documents asyncio.TimeoutError), or the wait_for result/cancellation races in listener_loop on 3.10/3.11. I did not read config.py, keys.py or _contradict.py in depth (sync code, almost no exception handling). Not read: element.py send_keys/send_file/set_value and other methods, and tab.py download/print_to_pdf/get_all_urls. Leads I checked and dropped: verify_cf after the input disappears via document replacement (worked in the probe); the query_selector '__last' stale-node flag (could not trigger 'could not find node' because DOM.getDocument did not invalidate ids); the class-level Browser._update_target_info_mutex shared across event loops (its body never awaits, so it is never contended); strict utf-8 decode in _read_process_stderr masking the 'Failed to connect' error and skipping stop() (plausible but needs non-UTF-8 stderr, not shown). Lower-value items I did not report: DownloadExpectation/BaseFetchInterception __aexit__ sending CDP commands that can mask the body's exception; Tab.mouse_click without try/finally leaving the button pressed if cancelled between mouse_down and mouse_up; Connection.aclose not clearing enabled_domains when the listener has already died. Known-issue sites were skipped as instructed.

findings.title: One event handler that raises when called (e.g. wrong arity) kills the Listener through an explicit re-raise, so commands already in flight hang
findings.bug_class: exception re-raised inside dispatch loop
findings.scenario: A user registers `async def on_target(): ...` (no parameters) via browser.connection.add_handler(cdp.target.TargetCreated, on_target) or tab.add_handler(...). _accepts_connection_argument returns False, so the loop calls callback(event), which raises TypeError synchronously while the coroutine object is created. findings.title: A command reply that fails to parse kills the Listener, and the send() waiting for it hangs forever (aclose() cannot release it either)
findings.bug_class: exception-handling / exception escapes a loop and hangs a caller
findings.scenario: Any tab.send()/connection.send() whose result the generated cdp parser rejects. This happens when Chrome's protocol differs from the bundled cdp: a required key is missing (KeyError), or there is a new enum value, e.g. a cookie sameSite value unknown to CookieSameSite (ValueError). listener_loop pops the Transaction from conn.mapper and then calls tx(**message) outside any try. Inside Transaction.__call__, cdp_obj.send(result) raises something other than StopIteration, and the exception leaves listener_loop, so the listener task dies. The Future is never resolved. It is already gone from mapper, so _fail_pending_transactions in aclose()/_detach_session can never fail it, and send() hangs forever. Its own explicit `raise ProtocolException('could not parse the cdp response')` also kills the listener instead of failing the tx. On the browser connection this also starves every flat-session tab, because no one reads the websocket until another browser-level send() creates a new Listener. Event parsing on the same loop does catch these errors (parse_json_event in try/except -> logger.info; continue), which shows the intended behaviour.
findings.why_tests_miss: tests/core/test_connection.py has one test (concurrent aopen). No test feeds a malformed or schema-drifted reply. Real-Chrome tests use a Chrome that matches the bundled cdp.

Call conn.send(cdp.target.get_target_info()) as a task, wait 3s, then call conn.aclose() and check that the task is still pending. Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/detect-B15/probe_tx_parse.py and probe_tx_parse2.py

The same happened for Storage.getCookies with sameSite 'SomeFutureValue': listener exc ValueError("'SomeFutureValue' is not a valid CookieSameSite"). probe_tx_parse2.py: 'after aclose(): send finished? False | tx in mapper: 0'. The only trace is 'Task exception was never retrieved' at GC. findings.title: Element.click() (and mouse_click/mouse_move/mouse_drag/flash/screenshot_b64) raises a bare Exception on display:none elements: get_position never returns None, so every 'not visible' fallback is dead code
findings.bug_class: wrong exception raised / caller's None-handling unreachable
findings.scenario: `btn = await tab.select('#hidden-button'); await btn.click()` on a display:none element, e.g. a hidden <input type=file> or a visually hidden checkbox. click() calls `await self.flash(0.25)` before the JS `el.click()`. flash() calls get_position(), and Chrome returns empty content quads, so get_position runs `raise Exception('could not find position ...')`. Its `except IndexError: return None` is unreachable, because quads[0] only runs when quads is non-empty. flash()'s `if pos is None: warn; return` never triggers, and the exception escapes click(), so the JS click, which would work on a hidden element, is never sent. mouse_click/mouse_move/mouse_drag ('could not find location ..., not clicking') and screenshot_b64 (documented RuntimeError) also get a generic Exception instead of their graceful branch or documented type.
findings.why_tests_miss: Click and mouse tests in tests/core (test_tab.py, test_keyinputs.py, test_frames.py, test_mouse.py) only use visible elements. Nothing exercises hidden or zero-size elements.
findings.repro_idea: Open the page data:text/html,<button id=hid style="display:none" onclick="window.c=1">. Run `await (await tab.select('#hid')).click()`: it raises Exception, and window.c stays undefined. document.getElementById('hid').click() works. Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/detect-B15/probe_hidden_click.py, probe_swallow.py

findings.title: Element.query_selector_all / query_selector silently swallow every ProtocolException except 'could not find node' (e.g. invalid selector -> [] / None)
findings.bug_class: swallowed error the caller needs
findings.function: Tab.query_selector_all / Tab.query_selector (the _node branch, reached from Element.query_selector_all / Element.query_selector)
findings.scenario: `box = await tab.select('#box'); await box.query_selector_all('span[[')` returns [], and box.query_selector('span[[') returns None. In the `except ProtocolException` handler, the `_node is not None` branch only handles 'could not find node' and has no else/raise. Any other DOM error falls through to `if not node_ids: return []` (or `return None`). The same invalid selector at tab level (`tab.query_selector_all('span[[')`) correctly raises ProtocolException('DOM Error while querying'). A selector typo or any other DOM error therefore looks like 'no such element', silently, for element-scoped queries.
findings.why_tests_miss: Tests only use valid selectors. No test calls an element-scoped query with a selector or node Chrome rejects for a reason other than a stale node.
findings.repro_idea: Compare tab.query_selector_all('span[[') (raises) with (await tab.select('#box')).query_selector_all('span[[') (returns []). Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/detect-B15/probe_swallow.py
findings.evidence: probe_swallow.py printed: 'tab.query_selector_all invalid -> raises ProtocolException: DOM Error while querying', 'box.query_selector_all invalid -> []', 'box.query_selector invalid -> None'. The query_selector equivalent is at tab.py:649.

findings.title: Element.apply drops JavaScript exceptions: a throwing function returns None, and the exception_details branch is dead
findings.bug_class: error dropped where the caller needs it
findings.scenario: `await elem.apply("(e) => { throw new Error('boom') }")` returns None, the same as a function returning undefined. Runtime.callFunctionOn returns (RemoteObject of the thrown error, ExceptionDetails). result[0] is always a truthy RemoteObject, so `if result and result[0]: return result[0].value` returns the error object's value (None). `elif result[1]: return result[1]` can never run. Callers built on apply (clear_input, React value setters, user scripts) cannot detect failures, while Tab.evaluate raises ProtocolException(errors) for the same JS.
findings.why_tests_miss: The only apply test (test_react_controlled_input.py:113) uses a function that does not throw.
findings.repro_idea: On any page: `await (await tab.select('div')).apply("(e)=>{throw new Error('x')}")` returns None. Compare with tab.evaluate of a throwing IIFE, which raises. Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/detect-B15/probe_swallow.py
findings.evidence: probe_swallow.py printed 'box.apply(throwing fn) returned: None' and 'tab.evaluate(throwing) -> raises ProtocolException (for contrast)'. Confidence is medium because the code may have meant to return rather than raise the details, but even that path is dead.

findings.title: expect_request/expect_response: two matching requests in one burst cause InvalidStateError in a handler task and make .response/.response_body belong to a different request than .request
findings.bug_class: unhandled exception in handler task (set_result on done future) + state overwrite
findings.scenario: `async with tab.expect_response(r'.*\.json') as exp:` while the page fires two matching fetches together, e.g. Promise.all([fetch('a.json'), fetch('b.json')]). Both Network.requestWillBeSent events are drained back-to-back. On Python 3.12+, wait_for/Queue.get do not yield when data is already buffered. The listener schedules _request_handler twice before the first task can call _remove_request_handler. Task 1 sets request_id=R1 and resolves request_future. Task 2 overwrites request_id=R2, then set_result raises InvalidStateError ('Task exception was never retrieved'). response_future then resolves with R2's ResponseReceived, so exp.request is a.json but exp.response/response_body are b.json. DownloadExpectation._handler and BaseFetchInterception._response_handler have the same unguarded set_result.
findings.why_tests_miss: test_tab.py expect_* tests navigate to a single matching URL, so only one event ever matches.
findings.repro_idea: Run a fake CDP peer that, after one reply, sends requestWillBeSent(R1,a.json), requestWillBeSent(R2,b.json), responseReceived(R1), responseReceived(R2) in one burst. Await exp.request and exp.response and compare the URLs. Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/detect-B15/probe_expect_race.py
findings.evidence: probe_expect_race.py (py3.13.16) printed: 'expectation .request url : http://x/a.json', 'expectation .response url: http://x/b.json | request_id: R2', "unhandled task errors: [\"InvalidStateError('invalid state')\"]". Not yet probed on 3.10/3.11, where wait_for's inner task may yield and hide the race.

findings.title: One shared ProtocolException instance is set on all pending transactions, and every send() appends its own command to it, so each caller's error lists other calls' commands
findings.bug_class: exception object mutated across callers
findings.scenario: Three concurrent sends are pending and the connection is closed (aclose(), session detach, browser.stop()). _fail_pending_transactions sets the same ProtocolException('connection was closed') on every tx. Each awaiting send() then does `e.message += '\ncommand:...params:...'` on that shared object and re-raises it. Every caller receives an identical exception whose message lists all three commands, and the list grows with the number of pending calls, so the error points at the wrong command.
findings.why_tests_miss: test_pending_commands_fail_when_connection_is_closed has only one pending command and checks only the type.
findings.repro_idea: Run a fake peer that never answers, start 3 sends, call aclose(), and print str() of each result. Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/detect-B15/probe_shared_exc.py

findings.title: (Outside B15's bug class, found while reading) Tab.__call__ passes text and selector to wait_for in swapped positions, so tab(text=...) never finds text
findings.bug_class: argument order (not exception handling)
findings.scenario: `await tab(text='Hello world')` calls `self.wait_for(text, selector, timeout)` positionally, but the signature is wait_for(selector=None, text=None, timeout=10). The text is used as a CSS selector ('Hello world' matches no element), the call polls for the full timeout and raises TimeoutError('time ran out while waiting') even though the text is on the page. tab(selector='button') only appears to work because DOM.performSearch also matches tag names.
